name: Lemon Yellow (Crayola)
lede: Lemon Yellow (Crayola) is a pale, named crayon shade of the older artist's color [[lemon-yellow|Lemon Yellow]], and it carries almost the same hex code as our [[pastel-yellow|Pastel Yellow]] article.

sections.title: A crayon box variant
sections.body:
Our color graph marks this as a Crayola-named variant of the long-standing artist's color [[lemon-yellow|Lemon Yellow]], citing Wikipedia for the crayon's place in the Crayola list [1]. Lemon Yellow itself traces back through Werner's 1821 chart and Ridgway's plates to the ISCC-NBS charts of 1955, but Crayola's own paler, creamier box shade is a separate, later naming, not a repeat of that history [1]. By computed ISCC-NBS block, this crayon's pale swatch lands as a light greenish yellow [1].

The color graph places this crayon shade almost on top of its own near-duplicate, [[pastel-yellow|Pastel Yellow]], at a distance of just 1.2 units, and close to [[pale-butter|Pale butter]] at 3.8 and [[dark-cream|Dark Cream]] at 3.8 as well [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale yellow in 7 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.03 percent, as photographed, with the within-painting lens finding it in 6, rarer than 73 percent of our named colors [2]. The earliest dated match on file runs back to 1513, long before any Crayola crayon existed; that floor marks the limit of a thin early archive, not proof the shade existed that early, since the match is a look-alike hue in an old varnished photograph [2].
